scope.description: Whole paraview application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Scientific dataset readers/sources, filters, arrays/temporal analysis, representations, rendering, writers and parallel/interactive visualisation.

coverage.rationale: Fifty is the rubric's several-central-families-with-substantial-gaps judgement. A connected data-analysis loop is authorable across dataset ingest, geometric/field transforms, sampling/temporal analysis, camera/representation setup and checked data/image publication. These useful families span more than one isolated task; they are not weighted by the number of proxy bindings. Major parts of whole ParaView remain incomplete: interactive/client-server sessions and linked selections, full view/animation lifecycles, in-situ/remote workflows, specialised domains and outputs beyond the verified publication subsets. Uneven depth across these families makes this estimate low-confidence; generated constructor coverage neither establishes workflow completeness nor native qualification.

scope.description: Curated scientific data pipelines and the typed generated native catalogue with publication and inspection.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Curated operations express domain tasks, but much generated catalogue authoring remains typed native properties; volume of bindings does not make intent abstraction uniformly high.

limitations: Generated declarations do not establish every reader/domain on real data; no arbitrary Python or programmable filters; MPI and specialised readers need their own qualification.

Editorial estimate from current contracts, guidance and completion evidence; no exhaustive native API denominator or new native acceptance was measured for this assessment. Qualification and runtime availability must be queried separately.
